status: experimental B2a candidate design derived from the protected B1.1 design; corrects defects D1-D4 only; not approved
coordinates: world metres: x east, z north (x = 4i - 3000, z = 4000 - 4j on the canonical 4 m grid); heights in metres
concept: The Weathered Glacial Sanctuary. A high, asymmetric massif: one dominant horn-like summit with three different arms. The north and east (lee) sides are cut by deep cirques with steep headwalls. The west and south-west (windward) sides keep a broad, scoured fjell plateau that ends in a steep escarpment. The south face holds a smaller hanging cirque that the walking route climbs beside.

summits.name: North Peak
summits.role: primary summit, short WSW-ENE summit crest

summits.name: Tarntind
summits.role: second summit on the south-east arm, seen right of North Peak from the south

summits.name: Vesttind
summits.role: third summit closing the west arm above the fjell plateau

summits.name: Nordhorn
summits.role: gendarme summit on the north arete

summits.name: Austtind
summits.role: minor top on the High Tarn rim

saddles.name: Western Col
saddles.note: D2 reconciliation: B1.1 authored N1 668 m with Vesttind 724 m (56 m prominence). Vesttind came out 735.8 m and is kept (summit hierarchy is protected), so the prominence intent (about 56 m) sets the col to about 680 m. 668 m would make Vesttind 68 m prominent, over-separating the west arm.

saddles.name: Skar notch
saddles.role: deep notch, the clearest break in the southern skyline

ridges.name: West arm (windward)
ridges.character: broad crest; steep cirque-cut north side, long gentle fjell to the south

ridges.name: North arm (lee arete)
ridges.character: narrow arete with a gap and a gendarme summit, steep on both sides

ridges.name: South-east arm (stepped)
ridges.character: summit, deep notch, second summit, then stepped shoulders down to the Cairn approaches

startCap.note: D2: B1.1 applied no end caps in its flank-variation branch, so this arm continued as a radial cone behind the summit and filled the Western Col (726 m at N1). The cap now ends it 30 m behind the summit.

ridges.name: High Tarn west rim
ridges.character: lower rim from Tarntind over the Tarn col to Austtind and on to the R1 rim

ridges.name: Vestfjell plateau shoulder
ridges.character: flat-topped windward plateau with a steep lee escarpment facing the south cirque

buttresses.role: south buttress of Tarntind, east wall of the hanging trough
south-west shoulder of North Peak between the south cirque and the Western Col; carries the summit route
north wall of the east cirque
divides the great north cirque from the north-west slopes

cirques.name: Great North Cirque
cirques.role: largest lee cirque under the North Peak north face; drains to the north coast

cirques.name: Tarn Head Cirque
cirques.role: east-facing cirque at the head of the High Tarn west inlet

cirques.name: Hanging South Cirque

cirques.name: Vesttind north corrie
cirques.role: small corrie under Vesttind; breaks the north-west flank

protected.kind: every cell with a water surface keeps R1 height
hero, tarn-ascent and other routes keep R1 height along their centrelines (60 m corridor)

drainage: Recomputed, not preserved. The great north cirque and the north-west corrie drain to the north coast. The Tarn Head Cirque drains east into the existing High Tarn west inlet source, so High Tarn keeps a fed catchment. The hanging south cirque drains south to the central trough approach. Dry closed depressions left by the authoring are removed with a priority flood (epsilon gradient) and reported.

route.text: B2a: the R1 peak-ascent is followed to where it enters the edited terrain, then a grade- and cross-slope-limited search reaches the Vestfjell shoulder viewpoint (primary hiking approach, hiking grade <= 0.30). From the viewpoint an explicitly optional summit scramble (grade <= 0.50) reaches North Peak. Steep traverses get a modelled trail bench.
route.viewpointNote: The viewpoint is the highest node on the south-west shoulder reachable within the primary limits (grade <= 0.30 on rendered triangle edges, side-slope <= 0.9, no cell steeper than 1.25), searched within 200 m of (-636, 2680). It is chosen deterministically by the build.

base.note: base = R1 (smoothed in the core) - lowerM * core * coastTaper * southTaper * eastTaper; the lowering fades out toward the south and east edges, where the fixed R1 boundary lies downstream, so the lowland drains through it instead of ponding

summitNote: S0 knots are authored at 892 m so that the composed, smooth-max-blended summit lands at about 900 m

terminals.note: D1 authored terminal profiles: (authored - R1) decays to 0 by smoothstep between the coast freeze (70 m) and the terminal length L, blended between nearby structures; separately before the protected windward-gully corridor.

outlets.name: Tarn-rim hollow outlet
outlets.note: D4: the 0.39 ha conditioned hollow between the south-east arm and the High Tarn rim gets a natural outlet (no new tarn).

revisionNote: B2a.1 = the one bounded corrective pass: the first B2a build (B2a.0) passed the seam limit but lowered the west arm beyond Vesttind by about 80 m (21 px on the Birchwood skyline) because the 520 m arm-west terminal reached inland past the protected Vesttind radius. The arm-west terminal is shortened to 380 m.
